business_scope.primary_industry_name: Double-Shot PBT Plastic Injection of Novelty Keyboard Keycaps

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national jurisdiction; no separate sub-state company register; Paris commercial court district recommended for registered office)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Codified Napoleonic tradition; commercial law codified in the Code de commerce; EU regulations directly applicable)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the French Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 26 November 2007, entered into force 2010)

Convention between France and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (1967, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (freedom of establishment, Articles 49-54; free movement of goods)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-59-1 and R. 561-1 et seq. (national AML/CFT framework implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843); Loi n° 2016-1691 of 1 December 2016 (Sapin II), Articles 138-142 (UBO register creation); Décret n° 2017-1094 of 29 June 2017 (UBO declaration rules); Code de commerce, Articles R. 123-220 to R. 123-235-1 (UBO filing with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); CMF Articles L. 562-1 et seq. (national asset-freezing).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the corporate shareholder's Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing (applicable where a UBO is a foreign legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / competent corporate registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961), followed by sworn French translation; if issued in a non-Convention state, Consular Legalization at the French Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and individual UBO identification sheet (full birth name, date/place of birth, nationality, residential address)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin, or French notaire if executed in France
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus sworn translation into French by a court-certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original recent utility bill or bank statement evidencing the residential address of each director (président) and significant shareholder (issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or issuing bank of the shareholder/director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sworn translation by a traducteur assermenté near the cour d'appel; Apostille not routinely required for non-official commercial documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Pouvoir) appointing the French incorporation representative (avocat or licensed domiciliation agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Signing shareholder/director before a notary of the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (if executed outside France); sworn French translation when needed for RCS filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors (président), and ultimate beneficial owners against: (1) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (2) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Council Regulations); (3) the French national asset-freezing list maintained by the Direction générale du Trésor under CMF Art. L. 562-1 et seq.; (4) the OFAC SDN list whenever USD-denominated or US-nexus transactions (Stripe/Shopify Payments) are anticipated; and (5) domestic and international PEP databases in accordance with CMF Art. L. 561-10 (customer due diligence) and Art. L. 561-10-2 (enhanced due diligence for PEPs). Although a commercial SAS is not itself an AML-obliged entity, the payment institutions (Stripe, Shopify Payments) and the opening bank will apply full CDD/EDD; the UBO declaration filed with the RCS is accessible to TRACFIN and to obliged entities under restricted-access rules. EDD, including source-of-funds verification, is triggered by any PEP status or high-risk jurisdiction nexus.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités des entreprises operated by the INPI (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), in conjunction with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) held by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce; availability search via https://data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) of a French SAS must be composed of Latin-script characters; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Japanese, Cyrillic) are not accepted for registration and require a phonetic or semantic Latin transliteration. The name must be freely available in the RCS, not misleading, and not contrary to public order or good morals. All legal documents and invoices must mention the legal form 'SAS' or 'Société par actions simplifiée'. Where a foreign-language brand (nom commercial) is used, a Latin-script variant must be registered and, per the Toubon Law (Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994), French must be presented with equivalent prominence in commercial communications addressed to French consumers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a common-law style pre-registration name reservation service; the denomination is examined at the time the incorporation dossier is transmitted via the Guichet Unique and is provisionally secured during the statutory examination window (normally 5-15 working days, extendable by up to 5 days where supporting documents require completion). If the Greffe rejects the name (confusing similarity, misleading character, prohibited token, or public-order violation), the incorporator may either file a remediation by resubmitting an amended denial-free denomination through the Guichet Unique or, within 10 calendar days of the notification, lodge a formal 'réclamation' against the INPI's refusal; further judicial recourse (recours en annulation) lies before the juge commis à la surveillance du registre of the territorially competent tribunal de commerce (e.g., Tribunal de Commerce de Paris). The 30-day figure used in this dossier represents the practical contestability window during which third parties holding prior trademark or business-name rights may oppose a newly registered name before prescription, and the maximum statutory delay between the mandatory JAL publication and submission of the complete incorporation file.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for low-risk administrative and e-commerce activities under Code de commerce Articles L. 123-11-2 and R. 123-167-1 et seq., provided the domiciliation provider holds a valid prefectural authorization (agrément préfectoral), a written domiciliation contract is concluded, and the contract does not exceed five years (renewable). A direct-to-consumer keycap business with third-party logistics (FBA or 3PL) may validly register its siège social at an approved commercial domiciliation address in France; however, the seat must be real and not artificially displaced, and material substance (inventory, purchasing, support) should remain traceable in France to preserve situs for VAT registration under CGI Article 209.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 5% annualized likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a micro-entity e-commerce SAS domiciled at a licensed virtual office; the exposure is driven by DGFiP VAT fraud-control campaigns and on-site verifications at domiciliation providers. The percentage rises to approximately 20% if the company claims export VAT zero-rating (CGI Art. 262) without complete transport and export documentation, or if the domiciliation provider's user portfolio is targeted in a generalized inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First registration filing fee — 'formalité de création d'entreprise' submitted via the Guichet Unique, covering RCS registration with the Greffe du tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (remittance collected through the INPI Guichet Unique)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff book of the French Ministry of Justice for greffes des tribunaux de commerce (approximately EUR 95-110 for a SAS, indexed)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory legal publication of the constitution notice (avis de constitution) in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) in the territorial department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily capped market tariff of JAL publishers (EUR 160-240 excl. VAT depending on length and département)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial domiciliation contract — 12-month first-year fee at an approved 'agréé' domiciliation provider (virtual registered office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation provider holding prefectural authorization (Code de commerce Art. L. 123-11-2)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 30-60 per month for a standard administrative domiciliation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SAS articles of incorporation (Statuts) and pre-incorporation legal opinion covering class rights, governance and transfer of shares
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark flat fee of EUR 1,200-2,400 for a standard single-member or multi-member SAS

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (traduction assermentée) of foreign corporate documents, passports, UBO identification sheets and address proofs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Expert-traducteur assermenté près la cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court-fixed tariff of approximately EUR 40-60 per source page; estimated 3-4 pages under this scope

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille authentication of the foreign corporate shareholder's Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document's jurisdiction of origin (e.g., Companies Registry / High Court)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff in the origin jurisdiction (approximately HKD 125 or equivalent per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO KYC and PEP/sanctions screening of shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners (database search plus RCS/INPI watch)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party AML data provider engaged by incorporation counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 80-120 per screened subject; estimated 2-3 subject profiles

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional bank account and payment-rail onboarding compliance support (KYC package for the opening bank, Stripe and Shopify Payments verification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French licensed payment institution or neobank (e.g., Qonto, Shine) and Stripe/Shopify compliance desks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for assistance with KYC/CDD package assembly and UBO evidence pack

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), principally Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 and R. 123-1 et seq.; SAS formation and governance are governed by the Code and the company's articles of association.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local commercial and companies registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce), with applications submitted through the national Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic application for registration in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS), submitted through the Guichet unique, supported by the signed articles of association and required declarations.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. Cash contributions must be paid up at least 50% on incorporation; the balance is payable within five years after registration. Cash funds are deposited with a qualified depositary, such as a bank or notary, and released after registration. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed at incorporation; an auditor for contributions (commissaire aux apports) is generally required unless the statutory exemption conditions are met and the shareholders unanimously elect the exemption. The USD fee figure is an approximate conversion of standard registry and beneficial-ownership filing charges; publication and ancillary charges are additional and may vary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions set out in the executed articles of association and acknowledges payment of the required initial portion of each cash contribution, subject to confirmation by the depositary. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full French address], effective upon registration. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed President (Président) for the term and on the terms specified in the articles of association, and is authorized to represent the Company and complete its registration. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed [any other statutory or delegated office, if applicable]. RESOLVED, that the President may execute and file all documents and make non-substantive corrections required by the competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the SAS articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders; a French notary is required only where the transaction or contributed asset legally requires a notarial deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft articles stating the company name, purpose, registered office, duration, share capital, share classes, contribution terms, management powers, and decision-making rules. Obtain signatures from all founders. Notarization is not generally required for ordinary SAS articles; signatures must be authenticated or documents legalized and translated where the filing circumstances require it.
required_dossiers: President's identity and acceptance of office
Contribution-in-kind report or unanimous exemption decision, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies or missing particulars, obtain any required certified translation or legalization, and execute amended articles before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualified bank, notary, or other legally authorized depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit at least 50% of subscribed cash capital into a formation account in the company's formation name. Obtain the certificate of deposit for the registration dossier. The depositary releases funds after production of the RCS registration evidence.
required_dossiers: Executed articles or draft articles accepted by the depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank compliance queries with source-of-funds and ownership evidence; if a bank declines onboarding, use another qualified depositary or a notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized journal for legal notices (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the prescribed incorporation notice and retain the publication certificate. Ensure the notice matches the articles on company name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, and President.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice and certificate before submission if any publication detail differs from the executed articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Guichet unique registration filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI-operated Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; processing and RCS registration by the competent commercial registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic RCS registration application, declarations of beneficial owners, supporting documents, and applicable fees through the Guichet unique. Upload legible signed documents and ensure the activity description accurately covers plastic injection and sale of keyboard keycaps.
required_dossiers: President's identity, non-conviction declaration, and parentage details where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the registry's deficiency notice within its stated deadline through the Guichet unique, upload corrected or additional evidence, and pay any requested supplemental fee. Appeal or seek registry clarification if a refusal is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, competent commercial registry, and relevant tax and social-security authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers, provide registration evidence to the depositary to release capital, maintain the statutory registers and corporate records, and confirm tax and social-security registrations appropriate to the company's activities and employees.
required_dossiers: RCS registration evidence or Kbis extract
Tax and employer registration information, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected or incomplete post-registration declarations through the relevant portal and preserve proof of submission; obtain professional advice where tax or payroll classification is disputed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general industrial operating licence is ordinarily required solely for custom plastic keyboard-keycap injection. The competent site regulator is the Prefect of the department, with technical review by the relevant DREAL or DRIEAT, under the ICPE regime where applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Installation classified for environmental protection (Installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement, ICPE): applicable declaration, registration, or environmental authorization under the French Environmental Code and the relevant nomenclature, including the polymer-processing classification where thresholds are met.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition écologique), acting through the competent Prefect and regional environmental directorate (DREAL; DRIEAT in Île-de-France).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site- and capacity-dependent. Determine applicability under the ICPE nomenclature, including the polymer-processing entry, and the Environmental Code environmental-assessment screening rules. A declaration, registration, or authorization may apply; a full environmental impact assessment is required only where statutory screening or project thresholds so require.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with applicable ICPE prescriptions, water-law requirements, local discharge consent, and waste-traceability rules. No single national numeric wastewater or VOC threshold applies to every facility; limits are set by the applicable order, permit, sewer consent, and process-specific requirements. Segregate and lawfully transfer plastic scrap, contaminated packaging, oils, and other regulated waste; control process emissions and maintain records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupation, verify planning and building-use permissions, fire-safety requirements applicable to the premises, and electrical and machinery conformity. A building permit or change-of-use approval may be required depending on the site. The employer must assess occupational risks, prepare and update the DUERP, provide required worker training and protective measures, and arrange statutory inspections of relevant equipment. No universal separate fire or structural-load certificate applies to every workshop; requirements depend on premises classification, works, and equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS entities register directly with DGFiP upon incorporation to obtain SIREN and SIRET identifiers. Foreign-owned entities follow identical process via guichet-entreprises.fr or impots.gouv.fr, submitting incorporation documents and obtaining VAT identification number (TVA) if applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD directive apply, with optional micro-BIC regime for qualifying small businesses.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing via Chorus Pro platform with digital fiscal stamps and API reporting for all B2B transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to goods exported outside the EU with proof of export and non-EU destination; intra-EU supplies qualify under specific conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims incur penalties up to 80% of evaded VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback of benefits applies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, as the French central bank within the Eurosystem; the European Central Bank is the competent monetary authority for the euro area. The French Treasury Directorate General of the Treasury and French customs authorities administer applicable external-payment reporting, trade, and foreign-investment controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general foreign-exchange control regime restricting ordinary current-account payments, trade receipts, dividend payments, interest, royalties, or service fees. The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, customs, beneficial-ownership, and foreign-investment rules. A French SAS may generally hold foreign-currency accounts, receive foreign investment, make cross-border payments, and remit distributable profits without prior central-bank approval. Dividend remittances require legally available distributable profits, required corporate approvals, appropriate withholding-tax analysis, and supporting accounting and tax documentation. Banks may require evidence of the underlying transaction, source of funds, tax residence, beneficial ownership, and sanctions screening before executing transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds to France, surrender them to a bank, convert them into euros, or convert a prescribed percentage. No general statutory conversion deadline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts, subject to contractual bank terms, accounting records, customs documentation, sanctions controls, tax rules, and applicable statistical or regulatory reporting. EU and French sanctions, dual-use restrictions, customs rules, and anti-money-laundering controls may restrict specific counterparties, jurisdictions, goods, or payment routes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and relevant regional Crédit Agricole bank
BPCE group bank, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne entity

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; capital-deposit availability subject to entity and branch policy

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for operating payments, collections, multicurrency balances, cards, and payment-service connectivity, subject to provider eligibility and risk appetite. An electronic-money institution or payment institution authorised in France or another EEA state may passport services into France, but it is not a bank unless separately licensed as a credit institution. Customer funds are generally safeguarded rather than covered by the French deposit-guarantee regime applicable to eligible bank deposits. Offshore digital EMIs without an appropriate EEA authorisation, passport, or French establishment cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services to French customers merely through an online interface. Fintech accounts may be unsuitable as the sole capital-deposit account for SAS formation or as the only account for regulated or higher-risk flows. Providers may impose transaction, country, currency, marketplace, chargeback, and reserve restrictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement for all directors to attend a bank branch physically. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank or payment institution can perform reliable customer identification, beneficial-owner verification, document authentication, sanctions screening, and risk-based enhanced due diligence. The bank may require a video interview, qualified electronic signature, certified documents, an in-person appointment, a French address, or a locally resident authorised representative. The legal representative and identified beneficial owners must be disclosed; a bank may require identification of directors, shareholders, signatories, controllers, and relevant representatives. Remote onboarding is institution-specific and is not guaranteed for a newly incorporated SAS owned by non-residents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ownership chain, nominee shareholders, bearer-like arrangements, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current French company extract from the Registre National des Entreprises or equivalent registration evidence; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart to the ultimate natural persons; beneficial-owner declaration; passports or national identity documents; residential-address evidence; director and authorised-signatory details; and a signed ownership and control certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder, parent, director, or beneficial owner from a higher-risk, sanctioned, restricted, or opaque jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry extracts for each foreign entity; constitutional documents; tax-residence certificates where relevant; certified identification; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memorandum; audited accounts or bank statements; transaction rationale; sanctions-screening results; ownership-chain evidence; and written explanation of all jurisdictions involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection inconsistent with the shareholder profile, company business plan, or stated economic activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or capital-increase documents; shareholder or board resolutions; bank transfer evidence; proof of source of funds; financial statements or tax returns of the investor; investment agreement; capitalization table; business plan; expected transaction volumes; and confirmation that funds are intended for share capital, share premium, shareholder loan, or another correctly documented category.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS with no operating history, no French commercial footprint, or projected international volumes disproportionate to the business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or registered-office evidence; website and product catalogue; supplier and customer contracts; Shopify, Stripe, or marketplace agreements; customs and logistics arrangements; projected monthly turnover; payment-flow diagram; countries of operation; expected currencies; inventory and fulfillment evidence; and management biographies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving high-risk countries, sanctioned parties, restricted goods, dual-use items, or unusual intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-customer and supplier due diligence; invoices; purchase orders; bills of lading; customs declarations; end-use and end-user statements; product classification; sanctions screening; export-control analysis; beneficial-owner evidence for counterparties; and documented escalation and approval procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between stated business activity and payment descriptors, including unexplained marketplace receipts, card settlements, crypto exposure, or third-party collections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed payment-flow map; processor agreements; merchant-account ownership evidence; reconciliation reports; customer terms; refund and chargeback policy; invoices; accounting records; explanation of third-party payments; and confirmation that regulated payment services are not being provided without authorisation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax, accounting, or corporate compliance information, including missing annual accounts, tax identifiers, or beneficial-owner filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIREN and SIRET evidence; VAT number where applicable; tax-residence information; filed corporate returns; annual accounts or opening balance sheet; accounting engagement letter; corporate approvals; current registry extracts; and evidence of timely beneficial-owner and statutory filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, pooled accounts, unlicensed payment intermediaries, or accounts held in a different entity's name.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy; account-ownership matrix; intercompany agreements; agency or collection agreements where legally valid; proof of licensed status of payment providers; reconciliations; corrective migration plan; and evidence that all future commercial receipts and disbursements will flow through accounts held by the SAS or authorised regulated providers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High card-refund, fraud, chargeback, or delivery-risk exposure associated with online sales.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product and delivery terms; customer-verification procedures; fraud controls; fulfillment and tracking evidence; reserve methodology; chargeback history; refund policy; insurance; supplier quality controls; and rolling cash-flow forecasts demonstrating liquidity for refunds and settlement holds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use an account held in the SAS's name or, during formation, a compliant capital-deposit account opened for the company under formation. Route funds through SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-SEPA currencies. Identify the remitter as the shareholder or documented lender and use accurate payment references such as share capital subscription, share premium contribution, or shareholder loan; France does not use a universal statutory foreign-exchange purpose-code system. For a capital contribution, provide the bank and depositary with the subscription form, shareholder or board resolutions, articles, capitalization table, proof of remitter ownership, source-of-funds evidence, and formation or capital-increase documents. Do not mix share capital, share premium, shareholder loans, customer receipts, and operating funds without accounting and contractual classification. The bank may request an LEI, SIREN, VAT information, beneficiary-owner evidence, and supporting documents under AML rules. Verify beneficiary name, IBAN, BIC, currency, fees, intermediary-bank requirements, sanctions status, and receipt reconciliation. Record the transaction in the statutory accounts and preserve transfer evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro suppliers within SEPA, use SEPA Credit Transfer with beneficiary-name and IBAN verification and invoice-based approval. For non-SEPA suppliers, use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly documented through an MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, with accurate originator, beneficiary, purpose, invoice, goods description, and intermediary-bank information. Use commercial documentary letters of credit where supplier, country, or performance risk justifies them; the bank may issue an import LC subject to agreed rules such as UCP 600, with documentary examination, margin, collateral, and sanctions review. Alternative instruments include documentary collections, bank guarantees, and open-account payments with dual approval. Match invoices, purchase orders, customs records, shipping documents, and payment amounts; screen counterparties and banks; retain evidence of import or export compliance; and avoid third-party payments unless contractually justified and approved. Shopify Payments and Stripe settlements should be reconciled to orders, refunds, fees, chargebacks, and the SAS bank account, with reserves and settlement delays incorporated into liquidity forecasts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorised bank or investment firm, documented under appropriate master terms and used for identifiable commercial exposures.
Currency swaps for management of recurring or longer-term currency liquidity exposures, subject to counterparty credit limits, documentation, valuation, collateral, and applicable EMIR requirements.
Foreign-exchange options, including collars, where commercially justified and approved under the treasury policy; premium, option risk, accounting treatment, and suitability must be documented.

Non-deliverable forwards may be used for currencies subject to convertibility or settlement restrictions where the counterparty can lawfully offer the product; settlement is normally cash-based and the company must assess local restrictions, sanctions, tax, accounting, and counterparty risk.
Spot foreign-exchange transactions for operational conversion and settlement.

Hedging with an EU-authorised bank or investment firm should be governed by written dealing authorities, exposure limits, confirmation procedures, valuation controls, segregation of duties, and counterparty limits. Depending on the entity, instrument, and counterparty, MiFID II classification, EMIR reporting, clearing, margin, risk-mitigation, and record-keeping obligations may apply. Speculative trading unrelated to genuine business exposure should be prohibited under the treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €10,000 and potential administrative strike-off
Late filing penalties, tax interest charges, and possible administrative sanctions including strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory if average number of employees exceeds 50, turnover exceeds €50 million, or balance sheet total exceeds €43 million

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual confirmation required; beneficial owner register must be updated within one month of any shareholding or control change

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 0-500 USD (company address or local domiciliation service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0-5,000 USD (voluntary audit fees only; none mandatory for most SAS entities)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (5% of eligible expenses), innovation status tax benefits, regional tax incentives

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year end (e.g. 30 June for calendar year, subject to extension)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Domestic SAS reports full turnover; non-residents adjust for French PE
Include only French source income for non-residents

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.75% per month of delay on tax due (min €50), up to 10% of tax due; additional 40% penalty for false declarations

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% within EU/EEA under EU Directive; 12.8% to third countries
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and DTA relief application through impots.gouv.fr or bilateral treaty channels
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0-25% (often 0% for related parties under treaties); Interest: 0-25% (reduced to 0% for related party loans in many treaties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 50,000,000 euros (consolidated group revenue threshold for local file and master file requirements)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mandatory under French Economic Substance Regulations for entities claiming tax benefits without sufficient local activities; requires core income generating activities in France

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful false declaration or concealment of income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution with up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to €500,000; civil penalty of 80% of evaded tax plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, possible imprisonment, and disqualification from corporate offices

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a company without real economic activities or employees in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of profits, denial of tax deductions, fines up to €500,000 or 5% of turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for unpaid taxes, potential jail time for fraudulent conduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain TP documentation or apply arm's length principle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €5 million or 5% of annual turnover; possible criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and imprisonment for intentional non-compliance
